messages:
anna: quick proposal: introduce a versioned routing-policy header (X-Redwood-Routing-Policy: policy=v2;tags=sla:gold,cost:low) that carries SLA tags + cost-priority. v2 lets us do better quota rollups across dedicated+fallback pools and surface expected billing in Console. thoughts?
kevin: sounds promising. main risk is SDK lift. TS/python/go all parse headers differently today. will this be additive or replace existing routehint?
anna: additive for now. v1 routehint stays. v2 is a structured policy blob. SDKs can opt-in to emit v2 and we can backfill telemetry to measure impact.
pri: console ask: if we add SLA tags we can show a per-tenant "expected SLA" column and an estimated cost delta when migrating routes. need simulation endpoint to re-run historical requests against v2 mapping.
tomas: SDK side note: the TS SDK bundles a tiny header encoder; bumping to v2 might require a major if we change export shape. proposing we keep runtime API identical and add a helper: `client.routing.policyV2(...)` so it's non-breaking.
kevin: PY client quirk: sync clients created in short-lived processes sometimes never flush metadata header if we rely on a background handshake. recommend explicit sync API: `client.emit_routing_policy()` for short-lived CLI use.
anna: good point. let's add both helper and explicit flush APIs in python + ts. go should have env var override `REDWOOD_ROUTING_POLICY=v2` for non-code changes.
pri: telemetry plan: emit event `routing.policy.version` with fields: `tenant_id`, `sdk_lang`, `policy_version`, `tags`, `token_estimate`, `route_resolved_to`. sample at 0.5% global, 5% in canary orgs. need to ensure no PII.
tomas: SDK implement notes: TS will default to v1; v2 behind feature flag `experimentalPolicyV2`. we'll include migration lint in devex quickstart.
ops-bot: FYI scheduled canary for policy-service v2 decode at 2024-05-02T02:00Z (job 9021).
devex-bot: reminder: add changelog entry + migration notebook for policy v2 (template available in /docs/migrations).
kevin: question about quotas: will we aggregate tokens per-policy-tag? e.g., sla=gold should be tallied separately? billing wants flexibility.
anna: yes config idea: console admins can map tags -> quota_bucket. default: all -> tenant default. We'll surface a UI to preview historical bucketing so customers can approve mapping before enforcement.
pri: UX ask: add a "dry-run bucketing" checkbox on the Console tile that runs the offline replay and shows delta % for each bucket. also add small inline help: "tags are advisory until enforcement date".
tomas: implementation risk: golang SDK currently parses routehint at startup from env and caches it. if we add structured v2 we must keep backward-compatible parse and prefer explicit API > env var > legacy. I'll add tests for precedence.
kevin: rollback plan: if after flipping flag we see >8% mismatch between billed tokens and predicted tokens for any tenant for 48h, auto-disable v2 for that tenant and open an incident. SRE to own automation.
ans: (typo) anna: also: one more wrinkle: third-party integrators that sit in front of our API (gateway customers) might rewrite headers. we need to detect header-scrubbing. telemetry event `routing.policy.scrubbed` when expected header missing + client reports policy_version.
pri: agree. add a console alert rule: "policy header scrub detected" that notifies platform and tenant owner.
anna: action items: 1) pri to draft telemetry schema + sampling in telemetry repo, 2) kevin to sketch SDK helper APIs for py/ts/go and PRs, 3) tomas to add precedence tests in go client, 4) jason from SRE to own rollback automation. i'll write RFC with timeline (telemetry-only -> opt-in -> warn-by-default -> flip).
kevin: I'll start TS + PY PRs today, link when ready.
pri: I'll drop initial schema + console mock in the ticket.
ops-bot: canary deploy success   policy-service v2 decoders live on canary-3, traffic 7%.
anna: nice. thanks all. we'll sync next Wed to review telemetry numbers.
